nodes.label: Compatibility: version breaking contracts and coordinate regeneration, both apps and release
nodes.norm_label: compatibility: version breaking contracts and coordinate regeneration, both apps and release

nodes.label: Revisit conditions: dependency direction change, async native boundary, independently versioned clients, new shared crate or service
nodes.norm_label: revisit conditions: dependency direction change, async native boundary, independently versioned clients, new shared crate or service

nodes.label: Specs are numbered NNNN-kebab-title.md in the folder mirroring the scope workspace; a replaced record is marked superseded; ADR 0001 stays the founding record
nodes.norm_label: specs are numbered nnnn-kebab-title.md in the folder mirroring the scope workspace; a replaced record is marked superseded; adr 0001 stays the founding record

nodes.label: Rollout: one change in fifteen ordered steps (rules, AGENTS.md, architecture docs, README, validator, delete docs/plans, scope files, spec 0001, knowledge graph)
nodes.norm_label: rollout: one change in fifteen ordered steps (rules, agents.md, architecture docs, readme, validator, delete docs/plans, scope files, spec 0001, knowledge graph)
nodes.rationale: The steps are ordered so the checks never point at a missing file.

nodes.label: Spec triggers for a smaller change stay in their owner files (service rules, dependency rules, architecture compliance, FFI conventions, ADR 0001 Revisit when)
nodes.norm_label: spec triggers for a smaller change stay in their owner files (service rules, dependency rules, architecture compliance, ffi conventions, adr 0001 revisit when)

nodes.label: Dependency rules
nodes.norm_label: dependency rules

nodes.label: Architecture overview
nodes.norm_label: architecture overview

nodes.label: ADR 0001: Native apps with a shared Rust core
nodes.norm_label: adr 0001: native apps with a shared rust core

nodes.label: New dependency edge needs an owning module, a use case and a test
nodes.norm_label: new dependency edge needs an owning module, a use case and a test
nodes.rationale: Edges are proposed with owner, use case and test; the policy check and an architecture decision are updated together, and transitive dependency and binary-size effects are reviewed.

nodes.label: Color selection, font scaling, layout and accessibility run natively (no shared renderer)
nodes.norm_label: color selection, font scaling, layout and accessibility run natively (no shared renderer)
nodes.rationale: JSON-to-native arrows are build-time only; each app keeps its platform's navigation, gestures and controls without coordinating a shared renderer, and there is no application server or runtime configuration service.

nodes.label: Rejected alternative: shared UI runtime
nodes.norm_label: rejected alternative: shared ui runtime
nodes.rationale: A shared UI runtime would move control of navigation and rendering away from the native frameworks.

nodes.label: A smaller change needs a spec only when it changes ownership, a contract or a dependency
nodes.norm_label: a smaller change needs a spec only when it changes ownership, a contract or a dependency
nodes.rationale: The triggers are named by the service rules, the dependency rules, the FFI conventions, the quality checks and the Revisit when list in the foundation decision.

nodes.label: Enforcement: REQUIRED_DOCS drops plans/README and adds scope/index; whether a row and a spec exist and came first rests on review
nodes.norm_label: enforcement: required_docs drops plans/readme and adds scope/index; whether a row and a spec exist and came first rests on review

nodes.label: Force: the validator requires docs/plans/README.md and does not know the scope index exists
nodes.norm_label: force: the validator requires docs/plans/readme.md and does not know the scope index exists

nodes.label: Workspace edge: mobile-ffi depends on foundation-core (std-only core)
nodes.norm_label: workspace edge: mobile-ffi depends on foundation-core (std-only core)

nodes.label: Proc-macro exports define the cross-language API; bindgen feature gates host CLI deps
nodes.norm_label: proc-macro exports define the cross-language api; bindgen feature gates host cli deps

nodes.label: AGENTS.md: Working in the mobile foundation
nodes.norm_label: agents.md: working in the mobile foundation

nodes.label: Agent workflow: before editing (locate owner, contract, callers, tests)
nodes.norm_label: agent workflow: before editing (locate owner, contract, callers, tests)

nodes.label: Agent workflow: before handoff (run checks, report commands and unverified targets)
nodes.norm_label: agent workflow: before handoff (run checks, report commands and unverified targets)

nodes.label: Agent workflow: during implementation (place change in owning layer)
nodes.norm_label: agent workflow: during implementation (place change in owning layer)

nodes.label: App trees do not import one another; core never calls platform UI
nodes.norm_label: app trees do not import one another; core never calls platform ui
nodes.rationale: Each app depends only on its own platform SDK, generated bindings, native theme and resources, keeping the two native clients independent.

nodes.label: Decision: two Cargo workspace members; dependency-free core exported through UniFFI to native apps
nodes.norm_label: decision: two cargo workspace members; dependency-free core exported through uniffi to native apps
nodes.rationale: The product needs independently native Apple and Android presentations with one implementation of shared behavior. Keeping contract types separate from the implementation lets the core evolve without leaking internal types; cost is that an API change touches the export, both binding snapshots and both app verification paths.

nodes.label: Recommendation: relabel the ownership matrix row to 'Architecture, decision records, scope and agent workflow'
nodes.norm_label: recommendation: relabel the ownership matrix row to 'architecture, decision records, scope and agent workflow'
nodes.rationale: Leaving the old label would keep the one word (ADRs) that sends a reader looking for ADR files.

nodes.label: foundation_core::hello (sole greeting formatter)
nodes.norm_label: foundation_core::hello (sole greeting formatter)

nodes.label: Greeting call flow: SwiftUI/Compose -> generated binding -> C ABI/JNA -> mobile-ffi -> foundation-core
nodes.norm_label: greeting call flow: swiftui/compose -> generated binding -> c abi/jna -> mobile-ffi -> foundation-core

nodes.label: Public contract: hello(name: String) -> String in crates/mobile-ffi
nodes.norm_label: public contract: hello(name: string) -> string in crates/mobile-ffi

nodes.label: Layer: design system (generated Swift/Kotlin values as shared visual vocabulary)
nodes.norm_label: layer: design system (generated swift/kotlin values as shared visual vocabulary)

nodes.label: Layer: native platform integration (Swift owns Apple services, Kotlin owns Android services)
nodes.norm_label: layer: native platform integration (swift owns apple services, kotlin owns android services)

nodes.label: Layer: native presentation (views render, adapt to appearance, handle events)
nodes.norm_label: layer: native presentation (views render, adapt to appearance, handle events)

nodes.label: Layer: resources and tooling (build-host validation and generation)
nodes.norm_label: layer: resources and tooling (build-host validation and generation)

nodes.label: Layer: shared Rust (core owns behavior, FFI crate maps exports)
nodes.norm_label: layer: shared rust (core owns behavior, ffi crate maps exports)

nodes.label: Follow-up: add docs/reviews/ to repository-structure.md when its first file lands
nodes.norm_label: follow-up: add docs/reviews/ to repository-structure.md when its first file lands

nodes.label: Architecture boundaries
nodes.norm_label: architecture boundaries

nodes.label: Documented capability boundary; adapters need an actual caller
nodes.norm_label: documented capability boundary; adapters need an actual caller
nodes.rationale: A native SDK callback may update presentation directly, but anything affecting a shared decision is translated at a documented capability boundary so the core decides. Adapters, ViewModels and services are only introduced once a real caller exists.

nodes.label: Single greeting as the minimal exercise of interop, linking, resources and display
nodes.norm_label: single greeting as the minimal exercise of interop, linking, resources and display
nodes.rationale: One greeting is enough to prove language interoperability, linking, resources and display before committing to additional services.

nodes.label: Recommendation: name no folder before it has a file
nodes.norm_label: recommendation: name no folder before it has a file
nodes.rationale: docs/reviews/ and similar are added to the repository structure when their first file lands, in line with real caller first.

nodes.label: SF Symbols and Android system icons are selected in native presentation
nodes.norm_label: sf symbols and android system icons are selected in native presentation
nodes.rationale: Platform-owned iconography stays in the native layer; only shared brand masters live in shared/assets with license, provenance and export command.

nodes.label: Knowledge graph (graphify-out/, kept current with /graphify . --update)
nodes.norm_label: knowledge graph (graphify-out/, kept current with /graphify . --update)
nodes.rationale: The tracked files under graphify-out/ are committed together with the change they describe, so the graph always reflects the files added, edited or deleted by that commit.

nodes.label: Agent workflow: before commit (run /graphify . --update, stage graphify-out with the change)
nodes.norm_label: agent workflow: before commit (run /graphify . --update, stage graphify-out with the change)
nodes.rationale: Updating the graph before committing makes the knowledge graph cover every file the change adds, edits or deletes; staging the tracked graphify-out files into the same commit keeps the graph and the change in one revision.

nodes.label: Never hand-edit generated files
nodes.norm_label: never hand-edit generated files
nodes.rationale: Generated native outputs are derivatives of tokens, shared copy, configuration and brand sources; changes go to the source and are regenerated so both platforms stay in step.

nodes.label: Generators consume neutral sources and never recover canonical values from native output
nodes.norm_label: generators consume neutral sources and never recover canonical values from native output
nodes.rationale: Generation is one-way so neutral sources stay authoritative; platform builds consume the source snapshots under version control.

nodes.label: Decision: keep generated source snapshots in version control and compare against fresh regeneration
nodes.norm_label: decision: keep generated source snapshots in version control and compare against fresh regeneration
nodes.rationale: Xcode and Gradle compile a reviewed contract directly; verification regenerates in a fresh directory and compares, while target binaries and SDK installations are ignored.

nodes.label: Pass representative values through both generated languages
nodes.community_name: CI Workflow and Spec 0003 Build Plan

nodes.rationale: The number of products settles it. nodes.label: Fixture shared/config/foundation.json: schemaVersion 1, defaultLocale en
nodes.community_name: Configuration Guide and Native Build Settings
nodes.norm_label: fixture shared/config/foundation.json: schemaversion 1, defaultlocale en

nodes.label: Bundle development locale fixed to en
nodes.community_name: Configuration Guide and Native Build Settings
nodes.norm_label: bundle development locale fixed to en

nodes.label: foundation.json: public build-time configuration (v1 schema)
nodes.community_name: Configuration Guide and Native Build Settings
nodes.norm_label: foundation.json: public build-time configuration (v1 schema)

nodes.label: Native build settings stay in Xcode or Gradle (deployment targets, bundle and application IDs, entitlements, manifest entries); product identity lives in Identity.xcconfig and identity.properties
nodes.community_name: Configuration Guide and Native Build Settings
nodes.norm_label: native build settings stay in xcode or gradle (deployment targets, bundle and application ids, entitlements, manifest entries); product identity lives in identity.xcconfig and identity.properties

nodes.label: Configuration guide
nodes.community_name: Configuration Guide and Native Build Settings
nodes.norm_label: configuration guide

nodes.label: Recommendation: the identity files stay native
nodes.community_name: Configuration Guide and Native Build Settings
nodes.norm_label: recommendation: the identity files stay native
nodes.rationale: shared/config/README.md keeps application IDs in Xcode or Gradle. One shared file read by both builds was the runner up; it would break that rule and tie the two platforms together.

nodes.label: Only public settings in shared config; secrets via native credential store or CI secret store
nodes.community_name: Configuration Guide and Native Build Settings
nodes.norm_label: only public settings in shared config; secrets via native credential store or ci secret store
nodes.rationale: Signing material and other secrets are provisioned outside the repository; native deployment targets, IDs and entitlements stay in Xcode or Gradle.

nodes.label: Unknown keys and unsupported schema versions fail the build check; version schema for incompatible changes
nodes.community_name: Configuration Guide and Native Build Settings
nodes.norm_label: unknown keys and unsupported schema versions fail the build check; version schema for incompatible changes
nodes.rationale: Strict validation prevents silent configuration drift; an incompatible change versions the schema, updates the reader and migrates every checked-in config together.

nodes.label: Checker review mode: senior code review of a GA feature with fresh eyes, ranked findings in docs/reviews; only in a new session that has not written, verified or discussed the implementation
nodes.norm_label: checker review mode: senior code review of a ga feature with fresh eyes, ranked findings in docs/reviews; only in a new session that has not written, verified or discussed the implementation

nodes.label: Evidence labels: fixture or native, with native only for a run with a real binary; a fixture pass is not native proof, and missing hardware, binary or signing is recorded BLOCKED
nodes.norm_label: evidence labels: fixture or native, with native only for a run with a real binary; a fixture pass is not native proof, and missing hardware, binary or signing is recorded blocked

nodes.label: Gate Document it: the lead runs the document skill with changelog over the feature's merge range and commits CHANGELOG.md
nodes.norm_label: gate document it: the lead runs the document skill with changelog over the feature's merge range and commits changelog.md

nodes.label: Gate Review it (GA features): review by a new checker session that has not seen the implementation, file in docs/reviews; Blocker or Major findings start a fix item; ticked when none remain open
nodes.norm_label: gate review it (ga features): review by a new checker session that has not seen the implementation, file in docs/reviews; blocker or major findings start a fix item; ticked when none remain open

nodes.label: Gate Test it: tester report done, branch merged, evidence check passes on main; may run alongside Verify it
nodes.norm_label: gate test it: tester report done, branch merged, evidence check passes on main; may run alongside verify it

nodes.label: Lead step 6: tick gate and merge (only the lead edits scope files; clean worktree, diff limited to ownership, merge --no-ff --no-commit, checks on main, commit, then tick one box per edit)
nodes.norm_label: lead step 6: tick gate and merge (only the lead edits scope files; clean worktree, diff limited to ownership, merge --no-ff --no-commit, checks on main, commit, then tick one box per edit)

nodes.label: Reviewer rule: the reviewer must be a different model family from every author in the change range
nodes.norm_label: reviewer rule: the reviewer must be a different model family from every author in the change range

nodes.label: shared/config, shared/localization, shared/assets: owner of public settings, locale content and brand masters
nodes.community_name: Brand Assets and Shared Resource Owner
nodes.norm_label: shared/config, shared/localization, shared/assets: owner of public settings, locale content and brand masters

nodes.label: shared/assets/ owns future brand artwork and its exports
nodes.community_name: Brand Assets and Shared Resource Owner
nodes.norm_label: shared/assets/ owns future brand artwork and its exports
nodes.source_file: docs/scope/_root/004 - Shared settings, text and brand assets.md

nodes.label: Android build, install and instrumentation checks
nodes.community_name: Brand Assets and Shared Resource Owner
nodes.norm_label: android build, install and instrumentation checks

nodes.label: Light and dark appearance verification in CI
nodes.community_name: Brand Assets and Shared Resource Owner
nodes.norm_label: light and dark appearance verification in ci
nodes.rationale: Each system appearance is set, the simulator is rebooted and the appearance re-read before the UI test runs, so both generated palettes are proven from independent boots; Android repeats the instrumentation suite with night mode off and on.

nodes.label: Records, typed errors, async calls and native callbacks have no caller or test yet
nodes.norm_label: records, typed errors, async calls and native callbacks have no caller or test yet

nodes.label: Generated drift remediation
nodes.norm_label: generated drift remediation
nodes.rationale: For generated drift, change the source, run the generator without --check, and review the entire diff rather than editing outputs.

nodes.label: Shared visual decisions and translations are generator inputs
nodes.norm_label: shared visual decisions and translations are generator inputs

nodes.label: Regenerate native projections in the same change
nodes.norm_label: regenerate native projections in the same change

nodes.label: Regenerate derived files alongside canonical inputs
nodes.norm_label: regenerate derived files alongside canonical inputs
nodes.rationale: The generated diff is reviewed for API, naming, locale or appearance changes.

nodes.label: Generated native strings owned by the resource generator
nodes.norm_label: generated native strings owned by the resource generator
nodes.rationale: Source and regenerated changes are included together so generated strings are never hand-edited.

nodes.label: Deferred: a contract beyond one string (record, typed error, async call)
nodes.norm_label: deferred: a contract beyond one string (record, typed error, async call)
nodes.rationale: The repository rules ask for a real caller first, so the first product feature is the place to prove records, typed errors and async calls. Needs a decision.

nodes.label: Follow-up: decide whether checks must pass before a change reaches main (branch rule or local hook)
nodes.norm_label: follow-up: decide whether checks must pass before a change reaches main (branch rule or local hook)

nodes.label: Follow-up: confirm or correct the inferred rationale
nodes.norm_label: follow-up: confirm or correct the inferred rationale

nodes.label: Follow-up: a small import scan in check-architecture.py for R3
nodes.norm_label: follow-up: a small import scan in check-architecture.py for r3

nodes.label: Follow-up: record reviewers per owner (CODEOWNERS) when a second contributor joins
nodes.norm_label: follow-up: record reviewers per owner (codeowners) when a second contributor joins

nodes.label: Force: coding agents are regular contributors and act on what they load
nodes.norm_label: force: coding agents are regular contributors and act on what they load

nodes.label: Force: generated files sit beside hand-written code (edits there are lost or hide a mismatch)
nodes.norm_label: force: generated files sit beside hand-written code (edits there are lost or hide a mismatch)

nodes.label: Force: one maintainer, so no second reviewer by default
nodes.norm_label: force: one maintainer, so no second reviewer by default

nodes.label: Force: two languages downstream of one source (a rule written in Swift and Kotlin drifts silently)
nodes.norm_label: force: two languages downstream of one source (a rule written in swift and kotlin drifts silently)

nodes.label: Four routes a value takes to a screen: Rust behavior via generated bridge, visual tokens via generator, text and settings via a second generator, per-app code
nodes.norm_label: four routes a value takes to a screen: rust behavior via generated bridge, visual tokens via generator, text and settings via a second generator, per-app code

nodes.label: Neutral: the first feature needing a record, typed error or async call across the bridge triggers R10 and a new spec
nodes.norm_label: neutral: the first feature needing a record, typed error or async call across the bridge triggers r10 and a new spec

nodes.label: Options considered were not documented; repository has no CODEOWNERS, no import boundary lint and no single contributing guide
nodes.norm_label: options considered were not documented; repository has no codeowners, no import boundary lint and no single contributing guide

nodes.label: Partly checked rules (R6, R7, R10, R12, R17, R19)
nodes.norm_label: partly checked rules (r6, r7, r10, r12, r17, r19)

nodes.label: Practices the standard replaces (duplicated Swift/Kotlin rules, hand-edited outputs, unpoliced dependencies, cross-app imports, speculative layers, copied literals)
nodes.norm_label: practices the standard replaces (duplicated swift/kotlin rules, hand-edited outputs, unpoliced dependencies, cross-app imports, speculative layers, copied literals)

nodes.label: Review-only rules with no automated check (R1, R3, R8, R9, R11, R14, R15, R16, R18)
nodes.norm_label: review-only rules with no automated check (r1, r3, r8, r9, r11, r14, r15, r16, r18)

nodes.label: Rule set R1-R19 (rule, owner file, enforcement)
nodes.norm_label: rule set r1-r19 (rule, owner file, enforcement)

nodes.label: Tradeoff: a direct push to main lands before a check can fail
nodes.norm_label: tradeoff: a direct push to main lands before a check can fail

nodes.label: Tradeoff: 'material' is a judgment call decided by the reviewer outside the written triggers
nodes.norm_label: tradeoff: 'material' is a judgment call decided by the reviewer outside the written triggers

nodes.label: Tradeoff: nine of nineteen rules rest on review alone, six more partly checked, one reviewer
nodes.norm_label: tradeoff: nine of nineteen rules rest on review alone, six more partly checked, one reviewer

nodes.label: Neutral: the ownership matrix grows to eleven rows and spec 0001 is amended in the same change
nodes.norm_label: neutral: the ownership matrix grows to eleven rows and spec 0001 is amended in the same change

nodes.label: Android rules
nodes.norm_label: android rules

nodes.label: Spec 0001: One owner per responsibility, with rules kept beside the code
nodes.norm_label: spec 0001: one owner per responsibility, with rules kept beside the code

nodes.label: Automate only what a machine can judge
nodes.norm_label: automate only what a machine can judge
nodes.rationale: Checks can detect drift or a missing document but cannot decide whether two algorithms mean the same thing, whether a document is accurate, or whether a boundary serves a real use; the validator is kept small for that reason (stated in the repository).

nodes.label: Decision: one owner per responsibility in an ownership matrix, topic-sized rule files, short AGENTS.md entry point, automated checks only where a machine is reliable
nodes.norm_label: decision: one owner per responsibility in an ownership matrix, topic-sized rule files, short agents.md entry point, automated checks only where a machine is reliable
nodes.rationale: Without a decision the first product feature would have to guess where shared behavior goes, when a new module is justified and which checks count as done. Every change starts at the single authoritative owner, and a new capability or a material ownership, contract or dependency change needs a written decision before code. Payoff: the governing file is two steps away (AGENTS.md, then the matrix or one rule file), hand edits to generated files fail the checks, a new crate or Cargo dependency is visible in the diff, and the foundation stays the size of what it proves.

nodes.label: An exact dependency list, not a deny list
nodes.norm_label: an exact dependency list, not a deny list
nodes.rationale: The validator compares each Rust crate's direct dependencies to a fixed set of names, so any new Cargo dependency fails until the policy changes in the same change. With one maintainer, that failure is the second reviewer (inferred).

nodes.label: A matrix before any rule
nodes.norm_label: a matrix before any rule
nodes.rationale: With two languages downstream of one source the first question is always where the thing lives; one table makes the answer a lookup, not a judgment (inferred).

nodes.label: R10: a new capability needs a scope row and a spec; a material ownership, contract or dependency decision needs a spec
nodes.norm_label: r10: a new capability needs a scope row and a spec; a material ownership, contract or dependency decision needs a spec

nodes.label: R19: a visual change is verified in light and dark and at larger text sizes
nodes.norm_label: r19: a visual change is verified in light and dark and at larger text sizes
nodes.rationale: CI runs the greeting in both appearances; nothing checks large text yet.

nodes.label: R1: each responsibility has one authoritative owner (the matrix lists eleven)
nodes.norm_label: r1: each responsibility has one authoritative owner (the matrix lists eleven)

nodes.label: R3: the two app trees do not import one another
nodes.norm_label: r3: the two app trees do not import one another
nodes.rationale: Enforced by review only; separate build systems (Xcode and Gradle) make a cross import hard, not impossible.

nodes.label: R7: presentation and OS integration belong to the owning app
nodes.norm_label: r7: presentation and os integration belong to the owning app

nodes.label: R9: search before adding a constant, rule, data shape, translation or asset
nodes.norm_label: r9: search before adding a constant, rule, data shape, translation or asset

nodes.label: Premise: rule files stay authoritative; the spec records the decision, rule set and enforcement, not a second copy
nodes.norm_label: premise: rule files stay authoritative; the spec records the decision, rule set and enforcement, not a second copy
nodes.rationale: A spec restating rules that already live in docs/ would be a second copy, which the standard itself forbids. When a rule changes, change its file first and update the matching row in the spec in the same change.

nodes.label: Small rule files, one topic each
nodes.norm_label: small rule files, one topic each
nodes.rationale: A contributor or agent changing Android packaging loads android-rules.md and nothing about tokens; this answers the force of agents acting on what they load (inferred from what shipped).

nodes.label: Premise: four coupled decisions in one spec (which names change, how a copy is made, what happens to inherited records, how updates arrive)
nodes.norm_label: premise: four coupled decisions in one spec (which names change, how a copy is made, what happens to inherited records, how updates arrive)
nodes.rationale: Each decision constrains the others and a split would let them drift. The risk is building update machinery before any product exists, so the spec decides only what cannot be changed cheaply after the first product starts and builds only what the first derivation calls. The first derived product is the real caller ADR 0001 asks for; the command that takes a later foundation release is described, not built.

nodes.label: ABI generation result (UniFFI 0.31.2, identical regenerated tree)
nodes.norm_label: abi generation result (uniffi 0.31.2, identical regenerated tree)
nodes.rationale: The check rejected an edited binding even with its original byte count and timestamp, showing the comparison is content-based; a Swift executable round-tripped a Unicode name and an empty name through the generated binding.

nodes.label: Rust rules
nodes.norm_label: rust rules

nodes.label: UniFFI generated files drift check
nodes.norm_label: uniffi generated files drift check
nodes.rationale: Builds a host library and matching CLI, regenerates Swift, header/module map and Kotlin in a temporary directory, and diffs the whole binding tree.

nodes.label: FFI shapes change in the annotated Rust export
nodes.norm_label: ffi shapes change in the annotated rust export
nodes.rationale: Kotlin and Swift are generated in one operation from the Rust export so the two clients cannot diverge.

nodes.label: Shared computations and validation belong in the core
nodes.norm_label: shared computations and validation belong in the core
nodes.rationale: A native view only decides how to present a validation result, so shared logic is not re-implemented per platform.

nodes.label: Regenerate both languages and run both apps after a signature or UniFFI upgrade
nodes.norm_label: regenerate both languages and run both apps after a signature or uniffi upgrade

nodes.label: Shared algorithms implemented in crates/core
nodes.norm_label: shared algorithms implemented in crates/core

nodes.label: Thin FFI exports with public contract tests
nodes.norm_label: thin ffi exports with public contract tests
nodes.rationale: Edge values are exercised at the core function; the exported contract is tested where type conversion can affect native callers.

nodes.label: UniFFI generator feature restricted to host tooling
nodes.norm_label: uniffi generator feature restricted to host tooling
nodes.rationale: Enabling CLI features in a production cross-build would pull in the generator dependencies.

nodes.label: R14: the UniFFI generator feature (bindgen) stays on host tooling
nodes.norm_label: r14: the uniffi generator feature (bindgen) stays on host tooling
nodes.rationale: Review only: the build scripts leave the feature off, and nothing stops a change to that.

nodes.label: R17: bridge hygiene (bindings match the library revision, no raw pointers, no hand-maintained C declarations)
nodes.norm_label: r17: bridge hygiene (bindings match the library revision, no raw pointers, no hand-maintained c declarations)

nodes.label: R4: shared behavior lives in the core, the export stays thin, both clients stay on one contract
nodes.norm_label: r4: shared behavior lives in the core, the export stays thin, both clients stay on one contract

nodes.norm_label: template placeholders: {name}, {date}, {foundation_url}, {ref}
